_comment: Copy to config.json and edit. chmod 640 the copy - it holds camera credentials.

paths._comment: frames_root needs room for ~2 days of frames. Point it at your largest disk.
paths._comment_state: state_dir holds capture.json and encode.json: what the daemons know that systemd cannot, such as whether the cameras are actually answering. A few KB, read by the web UI and by 'timelapse test'. Keep it on /var; it does not belong on the frames disk.

capture._comment: timeout_seconds must stay below interval_seconds. min_free_gb 0 disables the disk guard.

encode._comment: av1_preset p1 fastest .. p7 slowest. Lower cq/crf = higher quality, bigger files.

transfer._comment: Set enabled false to keep videos local. destination is a local mount path OR a remote rsync spec such as user@nas:/mnt/user/timelapse/
transfer._comment_cifs: On a CIFS/SMB mount, '-a' implies -o -g and rsync exits 23 because the share cannot set owner/group. Use ['-rt','--partial','--remove-source-files'] there. 'timelapse transfer' measures which flags your share accepts and writes them for you.
transfer._comment_mount: require_mountpoint refuses to transfer when the destination is not on a mounted filesystem - otherwise a dropped NAS mount turns into rsync filling your local disk. true checks the destination; a string checks that exact mount point, which is more precise.

_comment_notify: Optional nightly summary, to any number of sinks. Configure with 'sudo timelapse notify'. Types: discord (webhook_url), ntfy (server, topic, optional token), telegram (token, chat_id). The older top-level 'discord' block still works and is used when this list is absent, so configs written before 0.1.6 need no edit; when this list exists, that block is ignored.

discord._comment: Legacy, kept for configs written before 0.1.6. Ignored when 'notify' above is present.

web._comment: Optional read-only status page and video index. It never changes anything - no encode triggers, no camera control, no config edits.
web._comment_bind: 127.0.0.1 means only this machine can reach it, which is the safe value to hand-edit but rarely the useful one on a headless recorder. 'timelapse web' suggests this host's LAN address instead and checks that the address exists before writing it. There is no HTTPS, so anything other than 127.0.0.1 exposes the page to your LAN; put a reverse proxy in front for anything wider. Changing this needs 'systemctl restart timelapse-web' to take effect.
web._comment_auth: Optional single login. Leave auth out entirely, or leave either field empty, and the pages open to anyone who can reach the address, which is how it has always worked. Set it with 'timelapse web': the password is stored only as a PBKDF2 hash and cannot be read back, so a forgotten one is reset by running that again. What it is for: keeping the household or a guest out of the status page and the video index. What it is NOT: there is no HTTPS, so the password crosses the network in clear, and the video FILES stay reachable to anyone who knows their exact address. That last part is deliberate - it is what lets a saved .m3u keep playing in VLC after you log out.
web._comment_library: Leave library_root empty to work it out automatically: the transfer destination when transfer is enabled, otherwise paths.video_output. Set it when the videos are readable here under a different path - e.g. transfer sends them to a remote 'user@nas:/...' spec that is also mounted locally.
web._comment_state: state_dir is the ONLY directory the web UI may write to - it holds the sqlite index of your video library, and the cached update check. The systemd unit is scoped to exactly this path, so the videos, the frames and this config stay read-only to it.
web._comment_update: update_check asks api.github.com once a day whether a newer version is tagged, and only while someone has the Overview page open. It is the ONLY outbound connection this service makes. It sends no configuration, no camera names and nothing about your videos; GitHub sees this host's IP and the version string. Set false to disable it entirely.

_cameras_comment: name     -> used as the on-disk directory name; renaming orphans existing frames
enabled  -> false excludes the camera from both capture and encode
method   -> 'http' (snapshot URL, preferred) or 'rtsp' (persistent ffmpeg grabber)
keys starting with _ are documentation and ignored by the code
run timelapse_test.py before enabling anything, and again after any URL change

cameras.name: Driveway
cameras._note: Dahua-style snapshot CGI. subtype=0 is the main stream = full resolution; subtype=1 is the substream.

cameras.name: Doorbell
cameras._note: Reolink-style. Credentials go in the query string, so auth is 'none'. URL-encode any & # + % in the password or the URL parses wrong. 'rs' is only a cache-buster; any string works.

cameras.name: Garage
cameras._note: Per-camera overrides. interval_seconds and framerate default to capture.interval_seconds and encode.framerate; set either here and this camera alone uses it. A wide general view is fine at one frame a minute played at 30fps (1440 frames = 0:48 of video); a workbench wants a shorter interval. Omit them to follow the global settings, including when those change. The fetch timeout is clamped below whichever interval applies, and the keyframe interval follows the frame rate.

cameras.name: Backyard
cameras._note: Disabled example. Some cameras want basic rather than digest; if both fail with 401 but the URL works in a browser with no login, try auth 'none'.

cameras.name: Hallway
cameras._note: For cameras with no HTTP snapshot endpoint (e.g. TP-Link Tapo). Uses a supervised persistent ffmpeg at fps=1/interval. quality is ffmpeg -q:v, 2 = high.
